findings.title: Login form crashes when federated credential cannot be retrieved
findings.body: The bean calls credentialModelOpt.get() without checking whether RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) found a credential, and line 21 also calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without checking for an exhausted credential. For federated users, configuredFor/isConfiguredFor and getFederatedCredentialsStream are independent storage-provider operations: a provider can report the user as configured and validate codes while returning no credential model, or can return a credential whose codes are all used. In either case rendering the recovery-code login form throws NoSuchElementException instead of showing the form, potentially locking the user out.

findings.title: Successful federated recovery code is not consumed
findings.body: After credentialManager.isValid succeeds, this code only deletes the credential if the retrieved model already reports allCodesUsed(); it never persists a used state for the code that was just consumed. The storage implementation added by this PR likewise validates by checking whether any stored raw code equals the input and does not remove or mark that code, while its getCredentials method recreates every stored code as unused. Therefore, with the PR's federated implementation, the same recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, the prompt continues to request the first code, and the all-used regeneration path is never reached, defeating the single-use property of recovery codes.

findings.title: Creating codes in user storage leaves an existing local credential valid
findings.body: When updateCredential succeeds in user storage, the method only logs and does not remove or disable any recovery-code credential already stored in Keycloak's local database. This matters on upgrade and regeneration: before this change, recovery codes for federated users were always created locally, so regenerating them after the change creates a different set in user storage while the old local set remains. Credential validation can still accept credentials from either store even though getCredential prefers the federated set for display, so rotating recovery codes does not reliably invalidate the previous, possibly compromised, codes.

findings.title: No test for federated user falling back to local storage or for code consumption
findings.body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin covers only the branch where the test storage accepts the recovery credential and then logs in once using the first code. It does not cover a federated user whose storage rejects updateCredential and therefore must receive and use a local credential, nor does it verify that a used code cannot be reused, that the next requested code advances, that exhausted codes trigger regeneration, or that regenerated codes invalidate the old set. Those are the main new branches and security semantics introduced by the change, so regressions in them would not be caught.
